scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #4535: An IT Department user (it_hod, 192.168.1.2) reports they
cannot reach CS Department hosts (192.168.2.0/24) -- inter-department routing
between IT and CS seems broken. They suspect router0 (which connects both
segments) dropped one of its department interfaces or a static/RIP entry. Please
confirm the inter-department fault.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. router0 connects IT (192.168.1.0/24) and CS
  (192.168.2.0/24) and routes between them; it_hod reaches CS hosts (192.168.2.x)
  with 0% loss. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis of an inter-department routing fault that is not present.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- IT (192.168.1.x) cannot
reach CS (192.168.2.x) -- is NOT reproducible: router0's IT and CS interfaces
(192.168.1.1 / 192.168.2.1) are up, ripd is running, and it_hod reaches
192.168.2.x with 0% loss.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: inter-department routing is healthy and
the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the IT->CS path,
finds it working, checks router0's interfaces and RIP/connected routes, and
reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a dropped interface or a missing route to
satisfy the ticket is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The reported inter-department routing fault between the IT LAN (192.168.1.0/24)
and the CS LAN (192.168.2.0/24) does not exist in the current lab state. Every
component along the suspected path was inspected and found fully operational.

Router0's two department-facing interfaces are both UP and properly addressed:
eth0 carries 192.168.1.1/24 (IT segment via switch0) and eth1 carries
192.168.2.1/24 (CS segment via switch1). Both subnets appear as directly
connected kernel routes in router0's FIB and are enrolled in the RIP process
(version 2, networks 192.168.1.0/24, 192.168.2.0/24, and 10.0.0.0/8). There
are no iptables rules on router0 — all chains (INPUT, FORWARD, OUTPUT) have
policy ACCEPT and zero entries. The end-host it_hod (192.168.1.2/24) has its
default gateway correctly set to 192.168.1.1. Bidirectional end-to-end pings
across multiple IT↔CS host pairs (it_hod→cs_hod, it_hod→cs_lab1,
it_lab1→cs_lab2) all completed with 0% packet loss and sub-2 ms RTT.

Root cause: There is no fault — the premise of ticket #4535 is incorrect; the
inter-department path through router0 is healthy.

Corrective action: No network change is required. The helpdesk ticket should be
closed as a false alarm; the reporter should retest connectivity from their
workstation and escalate only if a localised host-level issue (e.g., incorrect
gateway on a specific PC) is observed.

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly notes router0's IT and CS interfaces are up with correct addresses, directly connected routes in the FIB, and validates inter-department routing with successful 0%‑loss pings, concluding no fault.

The agent's log shows concrete observations (successful pings between IT and CS hosts, router kernel routes for both subnets, host default gateway, and permissive iptables), and the conclusions follow directly from those checks. The investigation covers the essential elements to show the reported inter-department routing failure is not reproducible.
